flawed_step: The step "contract the triangle and lift back any 3-edge-colouring" assumes the contracted cubic graph G/T has a 3-edge-colouring. Nothing guarantees that. Lifting does work: if G/T is 3-colourable, the three edges at the contracted vertex get distinct colours, and each triangle edge can take the colour of the pendant edge on the opposite vertex. The converse also holds. So G is 3-edge-colourable exactly when G/T is. Contraction only reduces the question to a smaller bridgeless cubic graph, and that graph can be a snark.
counterexample:
Start from the Petersen graph P (outer 5-cycle 0-1-2-3-4-0, spokes i–i', inner pentagram 0'-2'-4'-1'-3'-0'). Replace vertex 0 by a triangle a,b,c, joined by a–1, b–4, c–0'. Call the result G.

G has 12 vertices and is simple and cubic. It is bridgeless: every triangle edge lies on the triangle, and every other edge lies on a cycle, because P is 3-edge-connected and any cycle of P through 0 lifts to G through a path in the triangle. G contains the triangle abc.

G is not 3-edge-colourable. Suppose it were. The triangle edges get three distinct colours. At each triangle vertex, the pendant edge must take the one colour missing there, which is the colour of the opposite triangle edge. So a–1, b–4 and c–0' get three distinct colours. Contracting the triangle back to vertex 0 then gives a proper 3-edge-colouring of P.

P has no such colouring. In a 3-edge-colouring, the edges of two colours form a 2-factor made of even cycles. P has girth 5 and is not Hamiltonian, so every 2-factor of P is two 5-cycles, which are odd. This is a contradiction, so G is a bridgeless cubic graph with a triangle and no 3-edge-colouring.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. Contracting a triangle keeps the graph cubic and bridgeless, and it preserves 3-edge-colourability in both directions. So it cannot create a colouring that was not already there. Blowing up one vertex of the Petersen graph into a triangle gives a 12-vertex simple, bridgeless cubic graph that contains a triangle but has no 3-edge-colouring, because such a colouring would give one of the Petersen graph.
